subject: physics
title: Radioactive Decay and Half-Life
welcome_lead: Watch unstable nuclei tick away exponentially with N = N₀ e^(−λt).
meta_desc: A-Level Nuclear adventure on decay law, decay constant and half-life.
final_note: Half-life and decay constant are linked by t½ = ln 2 / λ.

concepts.def: Decays per second, A = λN, measured in Bq.
λ = probability of decay per second.
Time for activity to halve: t½ = ln 2 / λ.
Each nucleus decays unpredictably and independently.

walkthroughs.body_html: Number of undecayed nuclei drops exponentially. Equally, activity A = A₀ e^(−λt). λ is the decay constant in s⁻¹.
Half-life t½ is the time for N (or A) to drop to half its initial value. After n half-lives, N = N₀ / 2ⁿ. Formula: t½ = ln 2 / λ ≈ 0.693 / λ.
Each individual decay is random and spontaneous, but with huge numbers of atoms the average follows the exponential law very closely.

mcqs.q: After one half-life, what happens to an individual radioactive nucleus?
options: Every nucleus is guaranteed to have half-decayed after one half-life.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.
It has a 50 percent chance of having decayed — radioactive decay is random for any single nucleus.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.

mcqs.q: Is radioactive decay periodic — does each nucleus decay at regular intervals?
options: Yes — half-life is the time between each emission from the source.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.
No — decay is a random process; half-life is a statistical property of a large population.
Yes — each nucleus 'ticks' at intervals of one half-life until it decays.

mcqs.q: Which type of nuclear radiation is most ionising?
options: Gamma is most ionising because it can travel furthest and pass through almost anything.
Alpha radiation — large, doubly charged particles cause the most ionisation per unit distance.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
